client.strengths: Practical skills (woodwork workshop), sense of humour, loyalty to his younger sister. Responds well to clear rules and concrete tasks.

justice.notes: Family court order placing him in the MOW (social maladjustment, truancy). No criminal proceedings.

client.strengths: A steady job (shift supervisor at a factory), organisational skills, an involved father. Told his wife about the debts and came to the clinic on his own.
client.supportNetwork: His wife (supportive but deeply hurt), a Gamblers Anonymous group, a therapist at the clinic, a colleague who has been through something similar.
client.family: Married for 18 years, two children (16 and 12). His late father had an alcohol problem. Conflict with his brother, from whom he borrowed money.
client.education: Technical secondary education (mechanic), with the same company for 15 years.

family.notes: A crisis of trust in the marriage after the debts came to light. The children feel the tension; the older son knows about the situation.

schoolWork.notes: Keeps his job but his concentration has dropped; he used to gamble during breaks at work.

peers.notes: Few close friends; earlier contacts were mainly through sports betting.

leisure.notes: Free time dominated by online betting and slot machines; gave up fishing.

health.notes: Insomnia, tension, “no way out” thoughts when the debts came to light – currently no suicidal thoughts, a safety plan agreed.

substanceUse.notes: Occasional alcohol, no signs of harmful drinking. Smokes cigarettes.

riskBehaviour.notes: Online sports betting and slot machines for 6 years, chasing losses, short-term loans hidden from his family.

justice.notes: No criminal cases; one debt collection case in progress.

riskFactors: Debts of about PLN 70,000 and pressure from debt collectors
Easy access to betting on his phone
The belief that he will “win it back” and repay the debts
Addiction in his family of origin
protectiveFactors: His wife’s readiness to work on this together
Strong motivation linked to his children
diagnosis.resources: An addiction clinic (behavioural addiction therapy), a GA group, free debt advice, blocking gambling transactions at his bank, the register of prohibited gambling domains.
diagnosis.conclusions: Gambling serves to regulate tension and escape problems; the debts maintain the “chasing losses” pattern. Priority: limiting access to money and games, a repayment plan, work on cognitive distortions and family support.

goals.title: Limiting access to gambling
goals.specific: Delete the apps, block gambling transactions and give his credit card to his wife.
goals.measurable: All blocks active; number of gambling-free days.
goals.achievable: His wife and therapist help set up the blocks.
goals.relevant: Access to gambling is the main risk factor.

goals.measurable: A complete list of debts, signed settlements, instalments on time.
goals.achievable: Free debt advice, a steady income.
goals.relevant: Debt pressure triggers thoughts of “winning it back”.

Debt advice appointment

goals.title: Rebuilding trust in the family
goals.specific: A weekly talk with his wife about money and a family session at the clinic.
goals.achievable: Therapist support, a group for families of people who gamble.
goals.relevant: His family is his most important reason for change.

note.conclusions: A safety plan and helplines agreed. Priority: blocks and first financial steps.

note.assessment: Action stage, high importance of change, low confidence.

meetings.homework: Write down 3 thoughts about winning and responses to them.

note.data: Identified distortions: “illusion of control” and “near miss”. Debt list complete.
note.assessment: Growing awareness of the mechanisms; first weeks without gambling.

meetings.title: Discussing the lapse

note.data: Confidence 6/10 (up). His wife agreed to come to a family session.
note.assessment: Stabilising after the lapse, better financial control.
note.plan: Next meeting: repayment plan.

client.strengths: Responsible, well organised, very involved in raising her children. Has a steady job (accountant) and a friend she trusts.
client.supportNetwork: A support group for family members at the clinic, a friend, her sister. Previously isolated herself so that “nobody would find out”.
client.family: Her husband (47) has an alcohol problem and is not currently in treatment. Her son (17) is in conflict with his father; her daughter (10) is withdrawn. During her husband’s drinking periods there are arguments and shouting.
client.education: University degree in economics, works as an accountant at an accounting firm.

keyDates.label: Parent-teacher meeting – son (at risk of failing two subjects)
End of the support group cycle

family.notes: Family life organised around her husband’s drinking; she takes over his duties and covers his absences at work. The children are burdened by the tension.

schoolWork.notes: Functions well at work, but takes overtime to “not be at home”.

peers.notes: Has limited social contact out of shame; keeps in touch with one friend.

leisure.notes: No time for herself; gave up her choir.

substanceUse.notes: Does not use alcohol or other substances.

riskBehaviour.notes: Controlling her husband (searching for bottles, checking his phone), giving in during arguments.

justice.notes: No proceedings. Informed about the “Blue Card” procedure and how to report violence.

riskFactors: Taking responsibility for her husband’s drinking
Risk of arguments escalating during drinking periods
protectiveFactors: A steady job and financial independence
A strong bond with her children
diagnosis.resources: The clinic support group, consultations for the children at the counselling centre, a crisis intervention centre, the municipal commission for solving alcohol problems.
diagnosis.conclusions: A pattern of over-responsibility and control maintains the family situation and exhausts the client. The work focuses on boundaries, self-care, safety and support for the children – regardless of her husband’s decisions.

goals.title: Handing back responsibility for the drinking
goals.specific: Not to make excuses for her husband at work and not to search for bottles.
goals.achievable: The support group, practised refusal phrases.
goals.relevant: Rescuing shields her husband from consequences and exhausts her.

actions.text: Practise refusing to call her husband’s workplace

goals.reviewNotes: Refused twice, once went back to the old pattern.

goals.measurable: Ticked off in a calendar; wellbeing scaling.
goals.achievable: Her sister will look after her daughter during that time.

actions.text: Rejoin the choir

goals.title: Safety and support for the children
goals.specific: Agree a safety plan and book a consultation for the children.
goals.achievable: The counselling centre, her sister’s support.
goals.relevant: The children are burdened by the situation at home.

familyPlan.familyStrengths: A close mother–children relationship, her sister’s support, financial stability, her son speaks openly about his feelings.
supportForFamily: Family members’ group at the clinic (mother)
Sociotherapy or a group for young people from families with an alcohol problem (son)
Municipal alcohol commission – information about the procedure for motivating her husband to seek treatment
familyPlan.safetyNotes: Arguments and shouting during drinking periods, no physical violence. Agreed plan: leaving with the children to her sister’s, emergency number 112, a domestic violence helpline. The “Blue Card” procedure discussed.
familyPlan.agreements: The mother does not take over her husband’s obligations towards his employer. Her son may go to a friend’s when tension rises at home and lets her know by text.

note.situation: Came after an argument at home that her son told his form teacher about.
note.behaviour: Spoke mostly about her husband and children, struggled to talk about herself.
note.emotions: Exhaustion, shame, fear for her children, anger suppressed by guilt.
note.relations: A strong bond with her children; control and tension in the relationship with her husband.
note.strengths: Responsibility, financial independence, readiness to work on herself.
note.conclusions: Offered the support group and a safety plan. Focus the work on her, not on changing her husband.

meetings.homework: Write down what she does for herself during the week.

note.data: Described her week: called her husband’s workplace twice, searched the cupboards daily. A safety plan was written.
note.assessment: Beginning to see what control costs her.
note.plan: Refusal practice, joining the group.

meetings.homework: One situation where she does not react by “rescuing”.

note.data: Attended two group sessions. Refused to call her husband’s workplace for the first time.
note.assessment: Relief and fear at the same time; her first experience of setting a boundary.
note.plan: Strengthen self-care – the choir.

meetings.homework: Call the choir leader.

note.assessment: Going back to control under strong fear – a natural part of change. Quick tension-reducing techniques are needed.
note.plan: 5-4-3-2-1 exercise, preparing a meeting with her son.

note.data: Wellbeing 6/10. She goes to choir; her husband called his employer himself. Her son agreed to come to a meeting.
note.assessment: Clear improvement in self-care and boundaries.
note.plan: A family meeting with her son, agreements in the family plan.

client.strengths: An active, curious class that works well on project tasks. A committed form teacher and class council.
client.supportNetwork: The form teacher, the school educator and psychologist, the parents’ council, the school nurse, a community youth club near the school.
client.family: 24 students (13 girls, 11 boys). Diverse family situations; several students from families facing difficulties receive individual support outside the programme.
client.education: Year 7 of primary school. The programme runs during form periods as part of the school’s educational and prevention programme.

keyDates.label: Presenting evaluation results to the teachers’ council

family.notes: Parents report little knowledge of e-cigarettes and of their children’s online activity.

schoolWork.notes: Good results and attendance; motivation dips towards the end of term.

peers.notes: Clear sub-groups, several incidents of exclusion in the class chat.

leisure.notes: Most free time spent on social media; about 40% of students attend after-school activities.

health.notes: More than half the students use their phone after 11 p.m.; frequent energy drinks.

substanceUse.notes: Survey: 21% have tried an e-cigarette, 12% alcohol; no regular use.

riskBehaviour.notes: Inflated normative beliefs – students think “most” peers use e-cigarettes.

riskFactors: Easy access to e-cigarettes and energy drinks
Weak skills for coping with pressure in the group and online
protectiveFactors: Good relationship with the form teacher
diagnosis.resources: Form periods, a room with a projector, the school educator and psychologist, municipal prevention funding, the community youth club.
diagnosis.conclusions: Universal prevention based on normative education and life skills, with a parent component, is indicated. Avoid scare tactics and one-off talks.

note.situation: First session during a form period, 22 students present.
note.behaviour: High engagement when creating the contract; several students withdrawn.
note.emotions: Curiosity, some amusement and distance at first.
note.relations: Visible sub-groups; the class council takes the lead.
note.conclusions: Work in mixed teams, involve withdrawn students through task roles.

note.behaviour: Great surprise at the results – students estimated that 60% of peers use e-cigarettes.
note.relations: The discussion cut across the class sub-groups.
note.strengths: Critical thinking, questions about data sources.
note.conclusions: Continue with the influence of advertising and social media.

note.situation: A session on digital hygiene and sleep.
note.behaviour: Students readily analysed their habits; several admitted to gaming late.
note.emotions: Engagement, some resistance to the topic of limits.
note.strengths: Their own proposal for a class challenge.
note.conclusions: The class took up the “phone out of the bedroom” challenge for 2 weeks.

note.behaviour: Role plays done with humour; refusing a close friend was harder than refusing a stranger.
note.emotions: Tension during role plays, then satisfaction.
note.relations: Mutual support, applause for shy students.
note.conclusions: Reinforce the techniques in a booster session.

note.conclusions: Prepare the summary and the post-survey.

note.situation: Closing session, survey completed by 23 students.
note.behaviour: Students prepared a poster with rules on their own.
note.relations: Better cooperation between sub-groups than at the start.
note.conclusions: Evaluation results show improvement; plan booster sessions.

prevention.title: “I know, I choose, I say no” – a universal prevention programme for class 7b
prevention.setting: A primary school in a medium-sized town, form periods.
prevention.needs: Pre-survey and the form teacher’s observations: e-cigarette initiation among some students, inflated normative beliefs, late-night phone use, tension in the class chat.
prevention.resources: The school educator (facilitator), the form teacher, the psychologist, a room with a projector, support from the parents’ council.
prevention.targetGroup: Class 7b students (24, aged 13) and their parents.
protectiveFactors: Bond with the school and the form teacher
prevention.generalGoal: Delaying nicotine and alcohol initiation and strengthening healthy digital habits among class 7b students.
specificGoals: Correcting beliefs about peers’ substance use
Increasing knowledge of how screens affect sleep
Supporting parents in talking with their children
strategies: Life skills development (assertiveness training, coping with stress)
Alternatives – a class challenge and after-school activities
prevention.budgetResources: Stationery and survey printing about PLN 150 (municipal prevention funding), the educator’s time within regular working hours.

indicators.label: Accuracy of beliefs about peer norms
Intention not to use e-cigarettes within a year
Knowledge of how screens affect sleep
Sense of belonging in the class
